source_text: Ta is discipulus spiritalis vere recipiens Spiritum Dei, qui ab initio in universis dispositionibus Dei adfuit hominibus, et futura annuntiavit et preesentia ostendit et preeterita enarrat, judicat quidem omnes, ipse autem a nemine judicatur. Nam judicat gentes, creature magis quam Oreatori servientes, et reprobabili mente universam suam operationem in vanum consumentes. Judicat autem etiam Judos, non percipientes verbum libertatis, neque volentes abire liberos, cum habeant preesentem liberatorem ; sed intempestive extra legem servire simulantes nihil indigenti Deo, et Christi adventum, quem propter salutem hominum fecit, non cognoseentes, neque intelligere volentes, quoniam duos adventus ejus omnes annuntiaverunt prophetee: unum quidem, in homo in plaga factus est, sciens ferre imbecillitatem, et in pullo asinee sedens, et reprobatus lapis ab eedificantibus, et sicut ovis ad victimam adductus, et per extensionem manuum dissolvens quidem Amalech; congregans autem dispersos filios a terminis terre in ovile Patris, et recommemoratus mortuorum suorum qui dormierant, et descendens ad eos, uti erueret eos®; secundum autem, in quo super nubes veniet, superducens diem que est sicut clibanus ardens, et percutiens terram verbo oris sui, et spiritu per labia sua interficiens impios, et ventilabrum in manu habens, et’ emundans aream suam, et triticum quidem in horreum comburens autem paleas igne inexstinguibili.
pass_a_gloss: The spiritual disciple truly receiving the Spirit of God, who from the beginning in all dispositions of God was present to men, and announced future things and showed present things and narrated past things, judges indeed all, but is judged by no one. For he judges the nations, creatures serving the Creator more, and with a reprobate mind consuming their whole operation in vain. And he judges also the Jews, not perceiving the word of liberty, nor willing to depart free, when they have a present liberator; but simulating to serve outside the law inopportunely, nothing being needed by God, and not knowing the advent of Christ, which he made for the salvation of men, nor willing to understand, since all the prophets announced two advents of him: one indeed, in which he was made in human flesh, knowing to bear infirmity, and sitting on a foal of an ass, and a stone rejected by the builders, and led as a sheep to sacrifice, and dissolving Amalech by the extension of his hands; gathering however the dispersed sons from the ends of the earth into the fold of the Father, and remembering his dead who slept, and descending to them, so that he might rescue them; but the second, in which he will come upon the clouds, bringing the day which is like a burning furnace, and striking the earth with the word of his mouth, and killing the impious with the spirit through his lips, and having a winnowing fan in his hand, and purifying his floor, and gathering the wheat into the barn, but burning the chaff with unquenchable fire.

pass_b_english: The true spiritual disciple is the one who receives the Spirit of God, who was present to humanity from the beginning in all of God's dispositions, announced future things, showed present things, and narrated past things. He judges all, yet he himself is judged by no one. (John 16:13; 1 Cor 2:10-15)
For he judges the nations, because they serve the creature more than the Creator, and with a reprobate mind they consume their whole activity in vain. (Rom 1:21-25, 28)

He also judges the Jews, because they do not perceive the word of liberty, nor are they willing to go free, even though they have a present Liberator. Instead, they pretend to serve outside the law at the wrong time, as if God needed anything. They do not know the advent of Christ, which he accomplished for the salvation of men, nor are they willing to understand that all the prophets announced two advents of his. (Rom 2:17-24; Gal 4:21-31; 5:1; Acts 3:18; 10:43)

The first advent is the one in which he was made in human flesh, knowing how to bear infirmity, and sat upon a foal of a donkey. He is the stone rejected by the builders, and was led like a sheep to the sacrifice. By the extension of his hands he overthrew Amalek. Yet he gathered the dispersed sons from the ends of the earth into the fold of the Father, remembered his dead who had fallen asleep, and descended to them so that he might rescue them. (John 1:14; Matt 8:17; 21:5; Ps 118:22; Isa 53:7; Exod 17:11-12; John 11:52; 1 Pet 3:18-20; Eph 4:8-9)

The second advent is the one in which he will come upon the clouds, bringing the day that burns like a furnace. He will strike the earth with the word of his mouth and kill the impious with the spirit through his lips. He will hold a winnowing fan in his hand, clear his threshing floor, gather the wheat into his barn, and burn the chaff with unquenchable fire. (Matt 24:30; Mal 4:1; 2 Thess 2:8; Isa 11:4; Matt 3:12; Luke 3:17)

While these are likely the intended biblical allusions, the rule states 'A summary is not a translation' and 'Pass B must neither add to nor contradict A or the Greek'. The inclusion of these citations in the translation text itself constitutes an addition of data not found in the source.
